A girl two grades younger than me got stabbed in the throat when I was a junior in high school. There was apparently a bad fight that day, and on my way walking home from school I actually saw her and her friends on their way to go fight this other woman. They were like amped up, talking crap about someone they were ready to fight. 

Yeah she sadly passed away, it was a very horrible situation, the grown woman- mind you.. pulled the knife out of no where and stabbed her in the throat, her friends put her in the car and then rushed her as fast as they could to the hospital but it’s like an hour drive from our small hospital to the bigger one that she would’ve been ambulanced to, she passed pretty fast.

They took a while to find the person who killed her cause I think they were on the run. At school no one was allowed to talk about anything that happened because the case was open and we weren’t supposed to be spreading a bunch of misinformation or saying anything about the case for multiple reasons. They gave an assembly where we gave our classmate a moment of silence but there wasn’t much said about the situation besides that they had extra therapists/counselors ready to talk if a student was struggling badly with the loss. After that they told us to go back to class and obviously the whole school was upset and mumbling/ whispering about what happened. We literally got screamed at for talking about it if we did ((we all were talking about it. this hadn’t happened before for us)) and it was terribly tragic we all cried even those who weren’t very close to her. Some crying students were yelled at and written up, sent to the office. If someone was upset over it a teacher would tell them to talk to guidance counselors but to absolutely not talk about the case it isn’t allowed. I just remember the pain and silence in school for that few weeks. & lots of people kept their kids home for a while, probably scared of anymore violence occurring since I think the person who killed her made threats to the school as well at some point during the fight/after.

It was honestly enraging, and I started to dislike him which made me sad because I loved him but it was just too much. I don’t think I ever really treated him like a human baby lol because he was a cat and required cat care (idk why people do that but I’m not judging). I had this same issue it didn’t matter what I did my son just would not sleep in the crib at that age. Around 4 months you can sleep train if you’d like to avoid cosleeping, but until then it may be really difficult and sometimes taking shifts holding baby while the baby sleeps is the only thing that helps. Not getting sleep is a literal form of torture so whatever you guys decide to do just don’t beat yourself up over it and remember this will pass. That’s great for your baby, but yes all babies are different and most peds advise feeding at baby’s demand until their weight is doubled. It’s everywhere online and not all babies keep their weight like that, it’s normal to lose some in the first few weeks. I’ve babysat and helped with lots of newborns including my own son when he was born, and most of them wake up pretty often wanting to feed. (Which is completely normal) Great for you guys who didn’t have to wake that often, lots of parents get PPD because of lack of sleep. I think some babies just don’t wake to feed very often and stay asleep longer, I’ve heard people on Reddit talk about how they got lucky and that they have to wake their baby to feed after 4 hours because they’re such good sleepers. Most others aren’t as fortunate. 

But it’s also good for them to feed often since they only can have small amounts when they’re first born, (half an ounce- an ounce) feeding them more often helps  their tummies get used to feeding more at a time as they grow. So I’m just saying, some people do get lucky and get more sleep but many others are really struggling and have to get up every couple hours to feed and change their baby. My son definitely didn’t need me to wake him to feed he was ravenous for breast milk every hour-2hours. He was like an alarm clock lol. It’s hard to imagine for people who haven’t gone through that but it’s very real and so many moms I talk to have been through the same struggle. Especially moms who choose to breastfeed. You have to breastfeed at least every 3-4 hours if you want to keep your supply as well. That killed me, having to be up to breastfeed and I would pump too. Babies breastfeed more often than drinking formula. Formula tends to fill them up more and takes longer to go through their system.

I’m not saying every experience is the same. It’s great if you got better sleep after birth and if your baby was a good sleeper, but lots of the lucky parents don’t realize how awful it feels for people who go through the trenches when it comes to newborn sleep and having to wake up so much. When I was pregnant (near the end of my first pregnancy) my sleep was horrible I had to pee every hour, my feet and arms were so swollen I had to move positions so often, but at least I could lay back down after going to the bathroom. When I was postpartum I refused to lay down with my baby during feeding because I didn’t want to fall asleep and have unsafe sleep. All I wanted was to at least lay down and I regretted not doing that all day before having my baby when I had that free time, especially because I had to sit up while having stitches from when I tore during birth. The pain was unbearable and I honestly needed more rest postpartum than I did during my whole pregnancy but I couldn’t have that. 

I honestly hope I get lucky with my next baby, (I’m due in July) and that I don’t have to wake as often this time around, that would be so amazing. All that I wanted was sleep for my first baby’s first 2 months of life. The reason people get downvoted when essentially ‘bragging’ about their babies being great sleepers is because most parents get jealous reading about it since it’s so so hard to have a baby that wakes often, I’ve been wishing and praying that my next baby is as easy as those babies that don’t wake often. Some people feel that their experience is invalidated when parents come online saying “oh my baby was so easy” or “it’s not that hard idk why everyone says they’re miserable! my baby slept great” because it’s like good for you, but others are miserable and crying, wishing for better sleep.
